click.sense: Pressing the mouse or trackpad button on a control (a button, a link, a badge), as opposed to pressing a key.
click.note: Many languages split this from pressing a key (es: hacer clic vs pulsar); a locale that uses one verb for both still records the choice.

coming-soon.sense: A marker on a feature or control that isn't available yet.

cost.sense: What something takes in money (AI usage) or in resources (disk space, a macOS process to suppress).
cost.note: Regional spelling splits (es coste / costo) are recorded per locale.

debug.sense: Troubleshooting detail for developers: a debug log level, saving logs for debugging.

direct-connection.sense: Cmdr's own fast SMB connection to a share, as opposed to the slower connection macOS mounts.

forget.sense: Removing a saved server, a saved password, or Ask Cmdr's saved notes, so Cmdr no longer remembers them.

history.sense: A record of past actions: the file-operation history, the Ask Cmdr chat history, a folder's navigation history.

originals.sense: The source files of a copy or move, kept or left where they were.

regex.sense: The regular-expression search and selection mode.

source-available.sense: Cmdr's code is public to read, under a non-open-source license (BSL).
source-available.note: Not open source: a translation must not claim an open-source license.

status.sense: The current state of something (a connection, a queue row, a sync app, a service page).

this-computer.sense: The user's own computer, named generically (not Mac) because the sentence also runs on Linux or means any machine.
this-computer.note: Regional vocabulary splits here (es ordenador / computadora / equipo); a locale records its pan-regional choice.

tint.sense: The faint background color that tells pane volume types apart (local, SMB/SFTP/WebDAV, MTP).
